system_prompt:
You are evaluated as a research and engineering assistant for Celestia, a traditional astrology application and separate prediction-research platform.

Rules:
1. Use only evidence in the current task. Never claim repository inspection, code execution, web research, API calls, tests, or deployment verification unless evidence explicitly shows it happened.
2. Never invent files, functions, code, test results, chart placements, planetary positions, calculations, citations, dates, API behaviour, or repository state.
3. Label material statements VERIFIED FACT, INFERENCE, or UNKNOWN.
4. If evidence is missing, say what is missing and how to verify it.
5. Do not silently change calculation conventions, public interfaces, saved-data formats, or existing behaviour.
6. Separate mathematical calculation from traditional astrological interpretation. Do not present astrology as scientifically proven prediction.
7. Prioritize correctness, reproducibility, regression safety, maintainability, and local-first operation.
8. Do not require paid services, paid APIs, paid trials, or proprietary dependencies. Prefer free/open-source alternatives.
9. Never request or reveal credentials, API keys, or private personal data.
10. If uncertain, say so. Do not fill gaps with plausible-sounding guesses.

Project context (not proof of current repository state): Next.js 15.4.9, React 19.2.1, Node.js 22.23.3; astronomy-engine 2.1.19 behind a facade named swissEphemeris (this does NOT prove native Swiss Ephemeris is installed); Vedic, Western, Jaimini, KP, BaZi, numerology, divisional charts, dashas, transits, relationship analysis, PDF output; saved profiles use localStorage key celestia_saved_profiles; KP confidence percentages may be heuristic. Calculation correctness has priority over feature expansion.

Follow the task's output schema exactly. If JSON is requested, return valid JSON only, with no Markdown fences or text outside the JSON.

A.prompt:
TASK A — CALCULATION & ASTROLOGY ACCURACY (COMBINED)

This is one task with three separately scored modules. Do not merge their conclusions.

MODULE 1 — CALCULATION INTEGRITY
Evidence:
- Project context: astronomy-engine 2.1.19 behind facade swissEphemeris.
- A previous audit raised a possible BaZi call-site issue: calculateBaZiProfile(year, month, day, hour) called without minute, timezone, or coordinates. This is an audit lead, not proof of a current defect.
- Previously supplied BaZi day-pillar reference fixtures: 15 March 2024 = Wu-Yin; 15 May 2024 = Ji-Mao.
- Historical timezone handling through Intl and a possible J2000 anchor discrepancy were previously raised.
- No current source, complete test logs, or runtime evidence is supplied.
Tasks: separate facts from leads; rank calculation risks; explain timezone/DST/longitude/minute precision; define independent validation for BaZi, Vedic, Western, divisional charts, dashas and boundaries; do not invent planetary positions.

MODULE 2 — ASTROLOGY SYSTEM KNOWLEDGE
Celestia covers Western tropical astrology, Vedic/Parashari, Jaimini, KP, BaZi, divisional charts, dashas, transits, relationships and numerology. No chart data is supplied.
Tasks: state minimum inputs and conventions by system; separate calculation from interpretation; handle cross-system disagreements without blending rules; explain birth-time uncertainty; give safe examples for placement, dasha, relationship, health and prediction questions; identify what cannot be known without chart data.

MODULE 3 — NUMERICAL REFERENCE FIXTURE
These are supplied reference longitudes, not values you need to calculate from the birth data. Convert to sign and degree within sign without rounding input:
Ascendant 343.925929°, Sun 256.863212°, Moon 306.468547°, mean Rahu 294.729703°.
Sign intervals: Aries 0–30, Taurus 30–60, Gemini 60–90, Cancer 90–120, Leo 120–150, Virgo 150–180, Libra 180–210, Scorpio 210–240, Sagittarius 240–270, Capricorn 270–300, Aquarius 300–330, Pisces 330–360.
Calculate absolute difference in arcseconds between ayanamsha 23.720706° and 23.717417°.

Return JSON only with exactly these top-level keys:
{"calculation_integrity":<MODULE 1 object>,"astrology_domain":<MODULE 2 object>,"numeric_fixture":<MODULE 3 object>}.
Use the nested structures exactly as specified by their object schemas. No Markdown or extra keys.

B.prompt:
TASK B — ENGINEERING, CODE AUDIT & TEST DESIGN (COMBINED)

One task with three separately scored modules. You have only the supplied repository excerpts; do not claim broader inspection or execution.

MODULE 1 — ENGINEERING REVIEW
Context only: Next.js 15.4.9, React 19.2.1, Node 22.23.3; astronomy-engine 2.1.19 behind facade swissEphemeris; localStorage key celestia_saved_profiles; KP confidence percentages may be heuristic; zero-cost/local-first preference.
Identify high-risk areas, explain why facade naming does not prove native Swiss Ephemeris, inspect data flow/timezone boundaries, propose safe minimal patches and rollback, protect localStorage migrations, and distinguish current recommendations from those requiring source evidence.

MODULE 2 — TEST ARCHITECTURE
Design unit/integration/property/regression/E2E/manual test layers; independent golden fixture governance; midnight, DST, historical timezone, approximate birth time, dasha boundaries and divisional rounding tests; release gates; explain what passing tests do and do not prove. Historical test reports do not prove current status.

MODULE 3 — SOURCE-GROUNDED CODE AUDIT
Evidence excerpts:
1. app/page.tsx parses birthTime into hour/minute but calls calculateBaZiProfile(year, month, day, hour); separately passes latitude, longitude and timezoneOffset to calculateWesternChart.
2. lib/astronomy/chinese.ts signature: calculateBaZiProfile(year, month, day, hour = 12); year pillar uses calculateYearPillar(year,month,day); month pillar uses calculateMonthPillar(yStem,month,day); day pillar uses calculateDayPillar(year,month,day,hour); hour pillar uses calculateHourPillar(dStem,hour). Solar month branches use fixed approximate day-of-month cutoffs. Day pillar advances when hour >= 23, then uses Julian day at 12:00.
3. lib/astronomy/swissEphemeris.ts imports astronomy-engine.
4. package.json lists astronomy-engine; supplied dependency manifest has no swisseph/sweph dependency.
5. scripts/testBaZiSuite.ts tests CompleteBaZiEngine.generateBaZiChart, not calculateBaZiProfile called by app/page.tsx.
State verified findings, risks, unknowns, coverage gaps, minimal safe patch plan, regression tests and claims not justified. Do not assert a bug beyond these excerpts.

Return JSON only:
{"engineering_review":<MODULE 1 object>,"test_architecture":<MODULE 2 object>,"source_code_audit":<MODULE 3 object>}.
Use the nested structures exactly as specified by their object schemas.
